To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have found evidence for a finite-size scaling relation for the 4th Binder cumulant for the SU(2) theory at finite temperature, that we have determined the critical exponents for this theory to be in the universality class of the 3D-Ising model, and that the corrections to scaling appear to be dominated, at least in the region of our data, by a term proportional, in lattice size, to the inverse of the fourth power.

(1) we find evidence that SU(2) in 3D is in the same universality class as the 3D-Ising universality class; (2) the corrections due to irrelevant operators are compatible with the breaking in the rotational symmetry; (3) the corrections to scaling are compatible with a term proportional to $\beta^3$; (4) the critical point of SU(2) is $\beta_c=2.2985(10)$.

the 4-th order Binder cumulant of a SU(2) pure gauge theory on $4\textrm{x}N_\sigma^3$ latices shows finite size scaling with $\nu=0{.637}(11)$. The corrections due to the breaking of the rotational symmetry are dominated by a term of the form $1/N_\sigma^{2.03(3)}$.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 4-th order Binder cumulant is a good candidate to study the critical behaviour in lattice field theories.
the SU(2) theory is a good candidate for the 3d Ising universality class, with the caveat that a better understanding of the corrections due to irrelevant operators is still lacking.

the 4th Binder cumulant on the lattice seems to provide a very good tool to extract the critical exponents in pure gauge theories, and that the 3D-Ising model universality is confirmed in the pure SU(2), SU(3) and SU(4) theories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
finite size scaling can be used to extract the critical exponents in a reliable way.
finite size scaling and universaltiy are not spoiled by the breaking of the rotational symmetry in the SU(2) pure gauge theory.
the 4th Binder cumulant is an efficient and accurate tool for the determination of the critical exponents of a gauge system.
